newsitem.title: UK: Store credit cards find favour with UK shoppers.
newsitem.headline: Store credit cards find favour with UK shoppers.

text.p: Shoppers in Britain spent 12.4 percent more using store credit cards in the first quarter of 1997 than in the same three months in 1996, according to figures published by the British Retail Consortium on Thursday.
The BRC said there was 2.8 billion stg outstanding on store cards at the end of the first quarter, an increase of 27.3 percent on the corresponding period in 1996.
The BRC's chief economic advisor Andrew Sentence said, "Rising spending on store accounts is one of a number of indicators of healthy consumer demand at present."
But he said the fact that much of the growth was coming from an increased number of accounts suggested that store card credit was displacing other forms of credit.
The number of retail credit accounts rose to 15.9 million, an increase of three percent over the quarter and 17.2 percent year on year.
The average account balance at the end of March was 174 stg.
The BRC's retail credit group, which produced the figures, represents more than 80 percent of the retail industry.
